clue.text: Return of service inaccurate, well out

indicators.note: a return sends something back, so the letters for the service are read from the end

parts.note: the RAF (Royal Air Force) is one of the armed services
a guess that is off is wide of the mark

explanation.surface: A tennis player's return of serve goes wide, landing well beyond the lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Something well out is distant, a long way away.

clue.text: Hard worker on land turning up in novel

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters are read upward, from bottom to top

parts.note: H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard
a serf was a feudal labourer bound to the land

explanation.surface: A farm labourer shows up as a character in a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses H + SERF to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Novel means new, original, never seen before.

clue.text: Arrives with bread and drink

parts.note: rolls are small loaves of bread
to sup is to drink in small mouthfuls

explanation.surface: Someone turns up bringing bread and something to drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls up is an informal phrase for arrives or turns up.

clue.text: Pick up food for a bird

parts.note: in cricket to field is to pick up the ball
fare means food, as in simple fare

explanation.surface: Gather some food to feed to a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: To field is to gather the ball in cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The fieldfare is a large thrush seen in Britain during winter.

clue.text: Virtually everyone has some reservation

parts.note: all means every person
but introduces a qualification or objection, as in 'no buts'

explanation.surface: Nearly the whole group agrees, though each has a slight misgiving.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtually means nearly or almost entirely, as in 'the job is nearly done'.

clue.text: Being a heel, I desert Louise

indicators.note: the letter leaves the name, abandoning it

explanation.surface: A man admits he behaved like a cad by walking out on his partner Louise.
explanation.definitionFit: A heel is a contemptible person; louse is a slang term for such a scoundrel.

clue.text: Insect on animal is a cause of annoyance

parts.note: bug is a general word for an insect
a bear is a large mammal

explanation.surface: A bug crawling on a bear irritates the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear is a persistent source of irritation or dread.

clue.text: Youngsters having seen great changes

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are changed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Young people who have witnessed huge social upheaval.
explanation.definitionFit: Teenagers are adolescents aged thirteen to nineteen.

clue.text: The salesman is untruthful in his answers

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
someone who lies is untruthful

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman gives dishonest responses to customers' questions.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers are responses to questions or letters, synonyms here.

clue.text: Did work badly -student chucked out

indicators.note: the student is placed within the word for chucked, taken as sitting out among its letters

parts.note: bunged is British slang for thrown or tossed
L is the learner plate, standing for a student driver

explanation.surface: Someone made a mess of the job, and a trainee was thrown out as a result.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNGED is informal British for chucked or tossed; L, the learner driver's plate, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To bungle is to botch, carrying out a task clumsily.

clue.text: There's a fish on the rod plain enough

parts.note: a pike is a freshwater predatory fish
a staff is a rod or pole

explanation.surface: An angler has a fish on the line, plain for all to see.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition comes from the idiom 'as plain as a pikestaff', meaning obvious.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'plain as a pikestaff' makes the word stand for obviousness.

clue.text: Plea for quiet before golf shot, it's a competitive game

indicators.note: the plea comes before the golf shot, putting it first in the answer

parts.note: whist is an old exclamation meaning hush or be silent
a drive is a long shot off the tee in golf

explanation.surface: A golfer asks for silence before teeing off in a tournament.
explanation.walkthrough: A WHIST DRIVE is a social card tournament, popular in Britain, where players move between tables.
explanation.definitionFit: A whist drive is a card-playing event in which players compete for prizes.

clue.text: There's no longer a morning paper

parts.note: ex means former, as in an ex-partner
AM stands for ante meridiem, before noon

explanation.surface: The morning newspaper has ceased publication.
explanation.definitionFit: A paper is a written test, as in an examination paper set at school.

clue.text: Copies returned, including one in colour

indicators.note: the word for copies takes another letter inside it
the word for copies is read from end to start

parts.note: apes means imitates or copies
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Photocopies sent back, one of them printed in colour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' turns APES into SEPA, and 'including' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown shade, familiar from old photographs.

clue.text: Deep displacement amidships from large troughs

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go among the letters of ships
the letters of deep are displaced into a new order

explanation.surface: Displaced water in the middle of the vessel comes from large tanks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'displacement' turns DEEP into EEPD, and 'amid' places it inside SHIPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheep dips are big tanks of insecticide through which flocks are driven.

clue.text: Compelled to use violence in the end

indicators.note: the violence word goes inside the word for the end

parts.note: end means the finish
to force is to use physical violence or coercion

explanation.surface: Someone driven at last to resort to brute strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Compelled means made obligatory, imposed by authority.

clue.text: Dismiss class mischief-maker

parts.note: to fire is to sack from a job
a brand is a kind or type

explanation.surface: Sack the class troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: A firebrand is an agitator who stirs up trouble.

clue.text: Ideal second choice?

parts.note: the fallback option after the ideal one, the one ranking just below the top

explanation.definitionFit: The runner-up option is what one takes when the first preference is unavailable.

clue.text: People in the wrong can cause distress

indicators.note: the people word sits inside the word for the wrong

parts.note: a tort is a civil wrong in law
men means people, persons

explanation.surface: Those who are in the wrong may upset others.
explanation.definitionFit: To torment is to inflict suffering or anguish.

clue.text: They're Moroccan musical phrases

definitions.meaning: the Rif people, also spelt with a double f, are Berbers of northern Morocco
short repeated melodic figures, as played by a jazz or rock guitarist

explanation.surface: Moroccan musicians play their distinctive phrases.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rif are a Berber people of the Moroccan mountains; in music a repeated short motif is the other sense.

clue.text: Disposition of uncle to have a fling

indicators.note: a disposition is an arrangement, so the letters are arranged anew

explanation.surface: An uncle's tendency to indulge in a brief affair.
explanation.definitionFit: To flounce is to fling oneself about, moving with exaggerated jerks.

clue.text: Down-at-heel wear for a rider

parts.note: shabby-sounding phrase really describes something a horse rider wears strapped low at the heel

explanation.definitionFit: A rider wears a spiked device at the boot heel to urge the horse on.

clue.text: Secure telephone provided for the explosive expert

parts.note: safe means secure, protected
the blower is British slang for the telephone

explanation.surface: A secure phone line is laid on for the bomb disposal specialist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The blower' is old British slang for the phone.
explanation.definitionFit: A safecracker who uses explosives to open strongrooms is an expert in blasting.

clue.text: Instrument for one in the performing arts

indicators.note: the letter for one goes inside the rearranged word
performing suggests the letters of arts put on a new show in a fresh order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An instrument for someone working in the performing arts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' turns ARTS into STAR, and 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The sitar is a long-necked plucked lute from India.

clue.text: A listener picks up two points and makes money

parts.note: an ear is the organ that listens
N and S are the compass points north and south

explanation.surface: A listener picks up some points and earns a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To earn is to gain an income through work.

clue.text: Statue with which one is too familiar

definitions.meaning: the Statue of ... in New York harbour

definitions.text: with which one is too familiar
definitions.meaning: taking this is behaving with undue familiarity or presumption

explanation.surface: A monument that someone treats with excessive familiarity.
explanation.definitionFit: The New York statue bears that name, and taking liberties means being overfamiliar.

clue.text: Where they wash and air French articles first

indicators.note: the French articles are placed at the front of the answer

parts.note: la is the French feminine definite article
un is the French masculine indefinite article
to air clothes is to dry them out

explanation.surface: A laundromat where clothes are washed and dried, French goods taken first.
explanation.definitionFit: A laundry is a place or business where clothes are washed.

clue.text: Heavenly body became a model on a vase

parts.note: a model sat for an artist
an urn is a decorative vase

explanation.surface: A figure posed for an artist painting a classical vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturn is a planet, an astronomical body in the sky.

clue.text: Those who do nothing but just tick over?

definitions.meaning: an engine that ticks over is running slowly without load

explanation.surface: Layabouts who merely keep themselves running at minimal effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Loafers are lazy people; engines idling run slowly, out of gear.
